intro: Sunday brings broader speech-recognition tests, sharper security scanning and a fuller picture of coding-agent use. Coastal storm disruptions continue, while city planning includes acoustic Beatles, practical AI discussions and two seasonal dining dates.

stories.title: Open ASR adds Egyptian and Nigerian English
stories.summary: Hugging Face’s Open ASR Leaderboard added two held-out conversational datasets supplied by Liva AI, covering Egyptian and Nigerian English. Developers can compare performance across more accents, including a new breakdown separating U.S. and non-U.S. speech.

stories.title: CodeQL trims false alarms and checks package boundaries
stories.summary: CodeQL 2.27.4 improves Java sanitization recognition and reduces false positives in Rust and C++ queries. Its command-line tools also exclude files whose symbolic links resolve outside a package’s root when bundling or publishing, warning maintainers about those omissions.

stories.title: Copilot dashboard starts counting chat engagement
stories.summary: GitHub’s Copilot impact dashboard now includes Chat and the VS Code Agents window, expanding its view to nine experiences. Enterprise and organization administrators gain corresponding 28-day reporting fields; these additions measure engagement without changing existing adoption-phase definitions.

stories.title: Second storm compounds outages and ferry cancellations
stories.summary: BC Hydro reported roughly 80,000 customers without power at Friday’s storm peak, while Saturday brought further ferry cancellations. The utility expects challenging weather through midweek; travellers should check sailing updates before heading to terminals.

stories.title: Police seek video after fatal Seymour Street collision
stories.summary: A woman died after an e-scooter carrying two people collided with a transit bus at Seymour and West Pender early Saturday. Vancouver police are investigating and ask witnesses or anyone with relevant video to call 604-717-3012.

stories.title: Business machinery spending falls for a second year
stories.summary: Statistics Canada’s new provincial accounts show business machinery and equipment investment declined again in 2025, despite a 14.1% increase in computer investment. Canada’s economy grew 1.9%, with household consumption and government spending supporting the annual expansion.

events.date: 2026-11-15 · 8 p.m. · Mel Lehan Hall at St. James, 3214 West 10th Avenue, Vancouver
events.title: Get Back Unplugged revisits late-period Beatles
events.description: Six Vancouver musicians reinterpret Beatles songs with acoustic instruments and five-part harmony, drawing on folk, Celtic, blues and jazz backgrounds. Doors open at seven for the all-ages concert; advance hall admission is $30, rising to $35 at the door.

meetups.date: 2026-12-01 · 6:30–8:30 p.m. · Parker Street Studios, 1000 Parker Street, Vancouver
meetups.title: Ethical Futures Lab turns recurring AI concerns into work
meetups.description: BC + AI’s December working session examines agency, accountability, labour, privacy and public trust through structured discussion and shared notes. Bring a laptop and a concrete question or example; registration requires approval, with a pay-what-you-choose checkout.

meetups.date: 2026-11-20 · 4–7 p.m. · FriendsQuarters, Unit 200, 116 West Hastings Street, Vancouver
meetups.title: AI Happy Hour offers time to compare notes
meetups.description: Builders, researchers, founders and other community members gather for informal conversation without presentations or a pitch circle. The $10 ticket includes one drink and earlier access to the members lounge for working; registration is required, with capacity capped at 60.

dining.date: 2026-11-13 to 2027-01-03 · Notch8, Fairmont Hotel Vancouver, 900 West Georgia Street, Vancouver
dining.title: Winter Wonderland tea opens Friday
dining.description: Notch8’s seasonal tea pairs cranberry-white-chocolate scones with smoked-salmon blini, turkey sliders and holiday pastries. Adults pay $79 before tax and gratuity; vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options require 48 hours’ notice. Check the calendar for excluded holiday dates.

dining.date: 2026-11-19 · 5 and 8 p.m. seatings · SUYO, 3475 Main Street, Vancouver
dining.title: SUYO and TOUK close a collaboration series
dining.description: SUYO’s Ricardo Valverde welcomes TOUK chef Chanthy Yen for a one-night menu connecting modern Peruvian and Cambodian cooking. Two dinner seatings are offered at $269 per person before tax and gratuity, with reservations directed through OpenTable.
